connections.why: Vectors are physical quantities carrying both magnitude and direction
Resolving force vectors is essential to applying the principle of moments
Free-body analysis resolves forces into components to find the resultant
The suvat equations describe the motion that resultant forces produce
Newton's second law links the resultant force to acceleration
Newton's second and third laws lead to conservation of momentum
Work done by a force is force applied through a displacement
Resistance relates the potential difference across a component to its current
A cell's internal resistance behaves like a resistor inside the source
Potential dividers split voltage in proportion to series resistances
Refraction is wave behaviour as speed changes between media
Lenses focus light by refracting rays at curved surfaces
Interference and diffraction arise from the superposition of waves
The photon model and de Broglie waves together define wave-particle duality
Photon energy and the work function are described in energy terms
Uncertainty analysis depends on understanding units and measured quantities
Internal energy and heat transfer extend the conservation of energy
Elastic strain energy is the work done deforming a material
SHM can be modelled as the projection of uniform circular motion
Gravity supplies the centripetal force that keeps satellites in orbit
Conservation of momentum analyses the scattering that reveals nuclear structure
An unstable nucleus undergoes radioactive decay
Binding energy per nucleon explains why fission and fusion release energy
Gravitational and electric fields share inverse-square field laws
A capacitor stores charge in the electric field between its plates
A magnetic field exerts a force that deflects moving charges
Accelerators steer charged particles using electric and magnetic fields
High-energy collisions in accelerators reveal fundamental particles
A2 uncertainty work extends the AS treatment to combined uncertainties
